'''Pan Junhua''' ({{zh|s=潘君骅}}; 14 October 1930 – 18 December 2023) was a Chinese [[applied optics]] engineer, and an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Engineering]]. He was a member of the [[Chinese Communist Party]].<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/>

==Biography==
Pan was born in [[Shanghai]], on 14 October 1930, while his [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] in [[Changzhou]], [[Jiangsu]].<ref name="Pan">{{cite news |author1=Song Hui ({{lang|zh|宋慧}}) |url=https://export.shobserver.com/baijiahao/html/695246.html |script-title=zh:苏州大学发布讣告：潘君骅院士逝世，享年94岁 |work=shobserver.com |date=20 December 2023 |access-date=9 February 2024 |language=zh}}</ref><ref name="Jun">{{cite news |author1=Wang Jianliang ({{lang|zh|王建亮}}) |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_25709716 |script-title=zh:中国工程院院士、著名应用光学专家潘君骅逝世，享年94岁 |work=thepaper |date=19 December 2023 |access-date=9 February 2024 |language=zh}}</ref> He attended the Wukang County Middle School and [[Shanghai Nanyang Model High School]].<ref name="Pan"/> In 1949, he was accepted to the Department of Mechanical Engineering, [[Tsinghua University]].<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/> After university in 1952, he was despatched to the [[Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics]].<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/> In 1956, he went to the [[Pulkovo Observatory]] in the [[Soviet Union]] to study astronomical optics and obtained an associate doctoral degree under the supervision of academician Maksutov ({{zh|s=马克苏托夫|labels=no}}).<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/>

He returned to China in 1960 and continued to work at the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics.<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/> In 1980, he was transferred to the Nanjing Astronomical Instrument Research Center, where he led the development of a 2.16-meter optical astronomical telescope, which earned him the First Class of State Science and Technology Progress Award in 1998.<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/> He became a researcher at the Institute of Modern Optics, [[Soochow University (Suzhou)|Suzhou University]] in May 2000.<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/>

In 2019, an [[asteroid]] with the international designation 216331 was officially named "Pan Junhua Asteroid" in recognition of Pan's significant contributions in the field of applied optics research for a long time.<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/>

On 18 December 2023, he died from an illness in [[Suzhou]], at the age of 93.<ref name="Pan"/><ref name="Jun"/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://new.qq.com/rain/a/20231220A08GZH00 |script-title=zh:沉痛悼念！潘君骅院士逝世 |work=qq.com |date=20 December 2023 |access-date=9 February 2024 |language=zh}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
* 1998 State Science and Technology Progress Award (First Class) for the 2.16-meter optical astronomical telescope<ref name="Jun"/>
* 1999 Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Engineering]] (CAE)<ref name="Jun"/>
* 1999 State Science and Technology Progress Award (Third Class) for the folded axis stepped grating spectrometer<ref name="Jun"/>
